visuals.heading: Reality Check Before You Decide

items.text: Every card includes a fit signal and a caution, read both before you commit.
Check the formal eligibility first: some roles still require a degree.
Whichever path you pick, do not let too much time pass without clearing these three checks, the exact point to check in depends on the path, but earlier is always safer than later.
If you cannot pass all three within a reasonable early stretch, the plan needs a rebuild, not more time.
One finished, shippable piece of work in your chosen lane, a deployed website, three real design case studies, a paid client project, or a cleared government-exam tier.
ITI, CS, coding bootcamps, and government exam prep all demand serious, structured study, often for years.
Mukesh Ambani, Azim Premji, Ritesh Agarwal, and Nikhil Kamath dropped out and built massive companies, but this is survivorship bias in its purest form.
A skill with zero live job postings or client demand in your target city or remote market is a hobby, not a career plan yet.

blocks.heading: Four Questions Before You Skip College

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: What can your family actually fund and for how long? A ₹60,000-3 lakh bootcamp plus 6-12 months of no income is a very different bet from a ₹15,000 ITI course that starts placement drives within a year.

figures.label: Total Course Duration
figures.source: If this specific skill-first path does not work out within 12-18 months, what is the backup, a related degree still on the table, a different skill, or a government-exam track running in parallel? A no-degree bet without a backup plan turns one slow year into a multi-year setback.

visuals.heading: Have This Conversation with Your Parents

items.text: "Without a degree, no company will even look at your resume."
"Just start a YouTube channel or become an influencer, degrees are outdated now."
"Everyone successful today dropped out of college."
"A degree is only a formality, it does not matter what you study."
Graduate unemployment in India sits at roughly 11.2%, more than three times the national average, and more than a third of graduates in their early twenties are unemployed.
Only about 42.6% of Indian graduates are considered employable, according to the Mercer-Mettl India Graduate Skill Index, drawn from 2,700+ campuses and over a million students.
82% of Indian employers say they struggle to find candidates with the right practical skills, meaning real, unmet demand exists for people who can prove capability.

blocks.heading: Degree-Only Myth Vs the Degree-Optional Truth

items.text: Doesn't explain why 11.2% of graduates are unemployed and only 42.6% are considered employable by industry standards.
Ignores that 82% of employers say the real gap is practical skill, not credential count.
Treats every degree as equal, when employability swings from roughly 58% to 78% depending on the field.

blocks.heading: Have This Conversation with Your Parents

items.text: Name the specific path, not "something in skills." "I want to do a full-stack bootcamp and become a developer" lands differently than "I want to try tech stuff."
Bring the real cost and real timeline.
Show one piece of current evidence.
Name your own backup plan out loud.
